page: Amazon Web Services g4ad.16xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor with 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core.

This instance is equipped with four AMD Radeon Pro V520 GPUs, delivering a total of 32 GB of VRAM. For local storage, the system bundles 2400 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. Networking capabilities are supported by a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in specific areas, with Passmark CPU, extended instructions, encryption, and database operations scoring in the top 25%. Geekbench ray tracing also registers in the top 25%. However, single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is in the bottom 10%, and large-model LLM text generation is in the bottom 25%. Most other memory bandwidth, compression, and medium-model LLM inference benchmarks fall within the middle 50% average.

The g4ad.16xlarge offers a balanced resource density for graphics-intensive and parallel processing workloads. The combination of AMD GPUs and local NVMe storage provides a cost-efficient alternative to other GPU instances for workloads such as ray tracing, database operations, and multi-threaded decompression. It is less suited for single-threaded tasks or large-scale LLM text generation.
